title: Decibels: Sound Pressure vs Signal Power
h1: Decibels — the same word for two different things
description: SPL dB uses 20 log. Power dB uses 10 log. Here is why sound and signal share a unit but not the math, and how to keep them straight.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against IEC 61672-1 and ANSI S1.4

hero: A 10 dB increase is 10× the power — or 3.16× the pressure. Whether you double or 10× depends on whether it is a power quantity or a field quantity.
body: The decibel is a ratio. The confusion is which ratio: power ratios use 10 log, field-amplitude ratios (voltage, pressure) use 20 log. Both give the same 'per bel of ratio' meaning because power is proportional to amplitude squared, so 10 log(P²/P₀²) = 20 log(P/P₀).

> Power dB: L = 10 × log₁₀(P/Pref)
> Field dB: L = 20 × log₁₀(A/Aref)
> Sound pressure level (SPL, dB re 20 µPa): 20 × log₁₀(p / 20 µPa)
> +3 dB power = 2× power. +10 dB power = 10× power.
> +6 dB SPL = 2× pressure. +20 dB SPL = 10× pressure.

20 microPascals is the human hearing threshold at 1 kHz. Every dB SPL number is referenced to it. 0 dB SPL = 20 µPa (threshold). 60 dB = conversation. 85 dB = OSHA action level. 100 dB = jackhammer. 120 dB = pain threshold. 194 dB = maximum possible in air (limited by atmospheric pressure).

The human ear is not equally sensitive at all frequencies. dBA applies a frequency filter matching low-level hearing (used for OSHA and traffic-noise regulation). dBC is flatter (used for peak measurements). dBZ is unweighted. A jet engine at 130 dBC may be 125 dBA — the two are not interchangeable.

Two identical machines each producing 80 dBA at 1 m. Combined SPL is not 160 dBA (never — dB is not a linear quantity to add). Instead: pressures add in quadrature. Each contributes 0.2 Pa; two contribute √(0.2² + 0.2²) = 0.283 Pa. That is 20 × log(0.283/20e-6) = 83 dBA — +3 dB above one machine. Doubling identical noise sources adds 3 dB, always.
Power dB: 10 log. Field/pressure dB: 20 log. SPL reference: 20 µPa. Doubling identical sources = +3 dB. 10× power = +10 dB = 3.16× pressure.

faqs.q: Is 40 dB twice as loud as 20 dB?
faqs.a: 10× the pressure, 100× the power, but only about 4× as loud perceptually. Human loudness roughly doubles every 10 dB.
Yes — anything below the reference. −10 dBm = 0.1 mW. Anechoic chambers reach −20 dBA SPL.

faqs.q: Why is dB SPL capped at 194?
faqs.a: At 194 dB SPL (~101 kPa peak), sound-pressure oscillation equals atmospheric pressure. Above that, the wave becomes a shock wave, not a sound wave.
